text:
maria: Quick convo: we need an operational policy for smoothing tenant spikes and handling orphaned token records before the next billing cycle. TL;DR: choose a deterministic per-event approach (bucketing) or a postprocess smoothing transform.

alex: My vote: deterministic bucketing at ingest. Pros: auditable, reproducible. Cons: changes aggregation dims and increases payload size slightly.

sam: Postprocess smoothing reduces event churn but obscures raw data. Auditors asked for raw, deterministic mapping. :thinking_face:

lee: Two additional constraints: cross-region ingest and replay/backfill. Whatever we choose must not break invoices if we re-ingest historical data.

maria: Proposal A (ingest bucketing): add `charge_window_ts` (server ISO), and `burst_shard` = hash(tenant_id) % N. `burst_shard` defaults to 1 (disabled) unless tenant opts-in. Example: N=4 for 15s subwindows inside 1m charge window.

alex: Implementation note: store `burst_shard` as tinyint, `charge_window_ts` as ISO string. Add documentation on how cost reports will group by `burst_shard`.

sam: Proposal B (postprocess smoothing): keep events unchanged, during billing aggregation redistribute high-volume tenant tokens into neighboring windows using a sliding window average. Pros: no schema change. Cons: non-deterministic unless we fix algorithm and seed.

lee: If we do B, we must publish the exact smoothing algorithm + seed and add audit logs for transformations. That still isn't as clean as A because the raw bucket is unknown.
maria: On orphaned tokens: observed corner cases where tokens are emitted but never linked to a request due to connector timeouts. Options: TTL GC (default 7d), immediate orphan ledger assignment (liability account), or aggressive stitcher.

alex: I prefer TTL GC + best-effort stitcher that annotates events with `reconcile_status` and `reconcile_confidence`. Keep default TTL 7d and allow per-tenant `orphan_ttl_days` override.

sam: Requirements for reconciliation events: must be flat fields (no nested objects) and include `reconciler_run_id`. Also emit `reconcile_action` = {"stitched","left_orphan","assigned_to_buffer"}.

maria: For replay/backfill safety: `charge_window_ts` should be set using the ingest service's server time at first write; replays must preserve original `charge_window_ts` (i.e., writers should not overwrite existing events). Backfills should be able to set a `backfill_origin=true` flag and provide an `original_ingest_ts` if available.

lee: We also need a consumer compatibility window. If we add these fields, downstream consumers get a 14-day compatibility window to handle both old and new schemas. Billing team: can you accept 14 days? @billing-bot

billing-bot: billing-team notified: compatibility window acknowledged. Will need CSV/schema changes and UX toggles.

alex: Performance note: adding `burst_shard` and `reconcile_*` fields increases message size ~+18 bytes avg; estimated cost 0.4% at 10B events/month. I ran a quick projection.

sam: Action items:
- Alex: draft schema PR for `charge_window_ts`, `burst_shard` (opt-in), `reconcile_status`, `reconcile_confidence`, `reconciler_run_id`, `backfill_origin`, `original_ingest_ts`. Put sample Avro/JSON schema in PR.
- Lee: spec consumer compatibility plan + 14d rollout plan.
- Maria: coordinate with billing for UI signals and per-tenant opt-in toggles.

maria: Quick poll: default orphan TTL 7d and default bucketing off (opt-in) — objections?

lee: -1 unless invoices surface TTL and opt-in clearly.

alex: +1 with opt-in and TTL visible in invoices.

sam: +1, will add reconciliation audibility requirements to the runbook.

billing-bot: deploy-checklist posted: schema-migration, consumer-compatibility (14d), backfill-tools scaffold, telemetry for cost delta.

maria: I'll open the RFC follow-up with the schema draft and timeline. If no blockers by EOD Friday we begin schema PR and opt-in rollout. Thanks all.
